_comment: Curated A19 test-point data. Hand-authored from the service manuals rather than
parsed, because Table 2-2 and the board disagree in two ways no parser should
guess at:
1. The -12 VOLTS row prints its nominal as '12V' with the sign dropped. Taken
literally the tool would tell a technician to expect +12 V on the -12 V rail.
TP10 is signed here and carries a 'conflict' saying so.
2. The silkscreen has thirteen test points; Table 6-24 lists jumpers for only
nine (TP1-5, TP8, TP10, TP12, TP13). TP6, TP7, TP9 and TP11 are labelled
pads with no jumper fitted -- still probe-able, still worth placing, but not
BOM parts. They carry notInParts.
Table 2-2 publishes a value for five points only (TP2, TP5, TP8, TP10, TP12) and
names TP13 as COMMON. The five unregulated points and the two logic lines are
tabulated nowhere in the manuals, so they carry noPublishedValue rather than an
invented number -- with the derived order of magnitude in the note, marked as
derived. §2-24 is explicit that these points exist to check the unregulated input
voltages, so they matter on the bench even without a published figure.
Every value is referenced to COMMON (TP13): §2-24 says all of this assembly's
supplies are, and COMMON is the transformer centre tap for the +/-12 V pair.
'source' on every value says where it came from. Nothing here is inferred into a
nominal; the inferences are confined to notes and to data/a19.caps.json.

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: Unregulated reservoir voltage on C1, ahead of the Q1/Q3 pass pair. The manuals tabulate no value for it — Table 2-2 lists only the regulated outputs. It has to sit above the 73 V output by the pass stage's headroom, and R6 (10 k, 2 W) across it dissipates 1 W at 100 V, so the design point is around 100 V; treat that as an order of magnitude, not an expectation. §2-24 names these unregulated points as the place to check the transformer's input to each supply.

73 V and not 75 V is the circuit rather than a typo: VR6 (36 V) plus VR7 (39 V) sets 75 V at the base of the Q3/Q1 Darlington, which then drops two base-emitter volts (§2-28). Reads near zero if the +35 V/+75 V shut-down circuit has tripped — check TP3 and TP6 before the regulator.

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: 75VSD, the display-refresh shut-down line, arriving from the Front Panel assembly (A2) on P41 pin 5C and pulled up to +5 V through R4. §2-29: low during normal operation; when the control display refresh fails it goes high, saturates Q10 and shuts both the +75 V and +35 V supplies down. The manuals publish no voltage for it, so this is a logic level rather than a reading.

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: Unregulated reservoir voltage on C3, ahead of Q5. No published value. It has to clear the 35 V output plus Q5's headroom, and R13 (10 k, 0.25 W) bleeds it, which puts the design point somewhere around 40–50 V. Order of magnitude, not an expectation.

Set by VR14 + VR15 (18 V each) driving Q5 as an emitter follower, with CR13 as the constant-current source feeding the stack (§2-27). Reads near zero if the shut-down circuit has tripped — Q8 removes Q5's base drive.

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: The CPU reset line, arriving on P41 (sheet 1 marks it PG1D7) and feeding Q9's base through R9. §2-29: low on power-up and during a CPU reset, which turns Q9 off and holds the +75 V and +35 V supplies down; high once the CPU is running. No jumper is fitted at this pad — it is a labelled probe point that Table 6-24 does not list.

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: Unregulated input to U1 (7812), on C6. No published value. A 7812 needs about 14.5 V in, and C6/C22 are 25 V parts, which puts the design point near 18 V. Order of magnitude, not an expectation. No jumper fitted at this pad.
U1 (7812) with heat sink. The +12V FAN line is the same rail taken through R7 (2 ohm) and L3, so a fan fault does not have to mean a regulator fault.

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: Unregulated input to U2 (7912), on C7. Negative with respect to COMMON. No published value; the same reasoning as TP7 puts it near -18 V. Order of magnitude, not an expectation. No jumper fitted at this pad.

testpoints.conflict: Table 2-2 prints this row's Nominal Output as '12V', unsigned, exactly as it prints the +12 V row above it. The rail is the negative one — the signal name is '-12 VOLTS', U2 is a 7912 and the schematic marks the net -12V — so the nominal is signed here. The printed cell is what the manual says; the sign is this dataset's correction.
testpoints.note: U2 (7912) with heat sink. The -12V FAN line comes off this same node through L6 only — unlike the +12 V side there is no series resistor in it (see the caveat on §2-26).

testpoints.source: Silkscreen and the sheet 1 test point legend
testpoints.note: Unregulated input to U3, on C12/C13. No published value. U3 is a low-dropout type and C12/C13 are 16 V parts, which puts the design point somewhere near 8–9 V. Order of magnitude, not an expectation. No jumper fitted at this pad.

5.2 V and not 5.0 V is deliberate: CR35 is a germanium diode between U3's ground pin and COMMON, and it lifts the output about 0.2 V (§2-25). Fitting a silicon diode in its place would put the rail near 5.6 V and is the first thing to check if this reads high.

testpoints.conflict: Table 2-2 and the board silkscreen call this point COMMON; the test point legend on schematic sheet 1 calls it GND. Same point.
testpoints.note: The return for every supply on the assembly, and the centre tap of the transformer's 12 V winding (§2-24). Reference every measurement on this board to it.

probePoints.label: P41 pin 5C — 75VSD in
probePoints.note: The display-refresh fault line as it arrives from the Front Panel assembly (A2). Same net as TP3. If TP3 sits high and the +75 V and +35 V supplies are shut down, this pin says whether the fault is coming from A2 or from R4/R11/Q10 on this board.

probePoints.label: U1 pin 1 — 7812 input
probePoints.note: Same net as TP7. Reach it here when the TP7 pad is obstructed; the tab of U1 is at COMMON, so the case is safe to lean a probe against.

probePoints.label: U2 pin 2 — 7912 input
probePoints.hazard: U2's tab is at the -12 V unregulated input, not at COMMON — the schematic says TAB TO INPUT. Do not let it touch chassis or a grounded probe barrel.

probePoints.label: U3 pin 3 — +5 V regulator input
probePoints.note: Same net as TP11. The +5 V regulator carries the whole logic load, so this is the node to look at when the instrument will not boot at all.

probePoints.label: R7, +12V FAN end
probePoints.note: The +12 V fan feed after its 2 ohm isolating resistor and L3. A fan drawing too much shows up as a drop across R7 that TP8 does not see.
